correlates.name: Lobar Pneumonia Localized by the Silhouette Sign
correlates.presentation: in the lecturer's case the right heart border is crisp but the left heart border cannot be seen — the patient has a lingular pneumonia.
correlates.pathophysiology: alveoli fill with pus, blood, or fluid, all of which are soft tissue density. Consolidated lung now matches the density of the structure it touches and the interface disappears.

correlates.name: Apparent Cardiomegaly on a Portable Film
correlates.presentation: the same patient imaged the same day has a normal cardiac silhouette on the PA film and an enlarged-looking heart on the AP film (Slide 21).
correlates.pathophysiology: projectional magnification, not disease — an anterior heart, a long heart-to-cassette distance, and a diverging beam.

correlates.name: Widened Mediastinum After Blunt Trauma
correlates.presentation: a trauma patient imaged supine with a portable AP film, reported as a "wide mediastinum.".
correlates.pathophysiology: a true mediastinal hematoma widens the mediastinal contour, but AP projection and patient rotation both widen it artifactually.

correlates.name: Tension Pneumothorax Missed on a Rotated Film
correlates.presentation: the film shows a pneumothorax; the degree of mediastinal shift is the finding that separates simple from tension physiology.
correlates.pathophysiology: air trapped under pressure in the pleural space shifts the mediastinum away from the affected side, obstructing venous return.

findings.name: Silhouette Sign
findings.represents: Loss of the expected interface between two structures of different density, because a structure is only visible where it abuts something of a different density
findings.territory: The left heart border is left ventricle abutting the lingula; the right heart border is right atrium abutting the medial segment of the right middle lobe
findings.association: Localizes a consolidation to whichever lobe touches the effaced border — the lecturer's first named must-know

findings.name: AP Projection
findings.represents: An anterior-to-posterior beam, used portably in the ICU or trauma bay, usually with the patient supine and the heart far from the cassette
findings.territory: Magnifies both the heart and the anteriorly-placed mediastinum
findings.association: Produces false cardiomegaly (mimicking CHF) and false mediastinal widening (mimicking hematoma) — check the label, not just the scapulae

findings.name: Poor Inspiratory Effort
findings.represents: Fewer than 9-10 posterior ribs visible above the diaphragm
findings.territory: Whole thorax, with the diaphragm riding high against the heart
findings.association: Produces false cardiomegaly by crowding the heart against an elevated diaphragm

findings.name: Underpenetration
findings.represents: A whiter film, in which the thoracic disc spaces cannot be made out behind the heart
findings.association: Misses retrocardiac masses and pneumonia hiding behind the cardiac shadow

findings.name: Overpenetration
findings.represents: A film so dark that the lung parenchyma is saturated out

findings.name: Rotation
findings.represents: Clavicular heads that are not equidistant from the spinous process
findings.association: Exaggerates the aorta into a false aneurysm or tracheal deviation, and under-represents mediastinal shift so a tension pneumothorax is missed

findings.name: Aortic Knob
findings.represents: The rounded contour of the distal aortic arch on the frontal film
findings.territory: Always on the left, the uppermost of the three left contour bumps above the pulmonary outflow tract and left ventricle
findings.association: The superior segment of a lower lobe can project as high as the knob — a classic localization trap

findings.name: Retrosternal Clear Space
findings.represents: The gas-filled space behind the sternum on the lateral film
findings.territory: Anterior mediastinum, invisible on the frontal film
findings.association: Should be entirely lucent; filling it means an anterior mediastinal mass

findings.name: Minor (Horizontal) Fissure
findings.represents: The fissure dividing the right upper lobe from the right middle lobe
findings.territory: Right lung only — the left lung has no minor fissure
findings.association: The only fissure visible on both the frontal and lateral films; the major fissure shows on the lateral alone

formulas.name: Radiographic Density Scale
formulas.equation: Air < fat < soft tissue/fluid < calcium < bone < contrast < metal
formulas.meaning: Density determines x-ray absorption and therefore film appearance, from air at maximum transmission (darkest) to metal at maximum absorption (whitest) — and pus, blood and simple fluid are all the same soft-tissue density
formulas.normalValue: A chest x-ray delivers about 0.1 mSv, roughly 10 days of the 3 mSv annual US background

formulas.name: Technical Assessment (P-I-P-R)
formulas.meaning: Four checks before reading any chest film — projection from the label, inspiration by counting 9-10 posterior ribs, penetration by just seeing the thoracic disc spaces, rotation by equidistant clavicular heads
formulas.normalValue: Each failed check produces its own predictable false finding

formulas.name: Lobes, Fissures and Segments
formulas.equation: Right lung: 3 lobes, 10 segments, minor and major fissures. Left lung: 2 lobes, 8 segments, major fissure only
formulas.meaning: The lingula belongs to the left upper lobe, not to a separate middle lobe, and it is what abuts the left heart border
formulas.normalValue: Right hemidiaphragm is seen entire; the left is effaced where the heart sits on it
